newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania vote grinds to conclusion after shooting.
newsitem.headline: Albania vote grinds to conclusion after shooting.

text.p: Albania's general election ground towards its second and final round on Friday as the already victorious Socialist Party and outgoing Democratic Party argued over who was responsible for violence at a monarchist rally in which one person was killed.

International troops moved in to guard the vote count headquarters a day after shooting erupted outside the building when Albania's pretender to the throne, Leka I, strode past wearing battle fatigues and armed with two pistols. A man in his 20s was killed.
The monarchists, who accused police of firing into the crowd, vowed to hold a new peaceful protest later on Friday and said Leka would attend, but this time would not don his fatigues.
They denounced what they called the rigged outcome of a referendum, which was held simultaneously with the first round of polling last Sunday, in which voters rejected restoration of the monarchy.

Officials of President Sali Berisha's defeated Democratic Party also said police fired at unarmed protesters. But a top electoral official inside said it was the protesters who shot first. Witnesses said most firing seemed to be into the air.
"There appeared to be, from eyewitness accounts, rounds fired into the crowd," Democratic Party Secretary General Genc Pollo told a news conference.
The early election was called to end months of violence in the Balkan country in which more than 1,500 people have died.

A 7,000-strong International Protection Force led by Italy has been helping to keep order since April and to protect polling stations. But Italy and Austria said on Friday they intended to pull out their troops by early August when the mandate for the force ends.
Election officials, pressed by Western monitors to produce final results of the first round quickly, announced that contests in 32 of 115 districts would go through to a run-off on Sunday.
The names of two finalists in each of the districts, where no candidate won 50 percent of the vote in last Sunday's first round, were sent to Italy for ballots to be printed.
Socialists were far ahead in seats declared, but officials gave no breakdown. An earlier tally gave the Socialists under economist Fatos Nano 49 seats to eight for the Democrats.
Berisha has said he will stand by a campaign pledge and resign once a leftist government takes power.
Local representatives of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which is overseeing the vote, said they were pleased that officials had come up with the lists.
"We are happy to have the names," spokesman Mark Smith said by telephone. "I think we can get ballots ready for the vote."
The OSCE had complained of interference in the count and said future aid to Albania depended on completing the election.

State television showed Albania's interim government, headed by Socialist Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, discussing Thursday's fatal shooting. It said Fino urged Berisha, party leaders and ordinary Albanians to avoid violence. Democratic Party representatives were absent.
Pollo and Tretan Shehu, Democratic Party chairman, accused the Socialists of inciting violence by disseminating false information about the outcome of the monarchy referendum.
They also suggested that Socialist Prime Minister Fino had dithered for two days in appointing an interior ministry, leaving the post vacant during the incident.

The new minister, Ali Kazazi, took up his duties on Thursday after his predecessor resigned. Both were members of Berisha's Democratic Party in accordance with the deal setting up the current interim government.

Leka's "court minister", Abedin Mulosmani, said monarchists were only defending their views. It was perfectly natural for the king, who has lived nearly all his life in exile, to carry a pistol and wear a uniform.
"I have seen him a thousand times dressed like that," he told reporters. "When he was born, (his father) King Zog put a revolver under his pillow."
